title: Receipt and invoice reader
audience: Small businesses, caterers and NGOs that log receipts in a spreadsheet
problem: A small catering business photographs every supplier receipt and types it into a spreadsheet by hand. Faded slips get misread and the same receipt sometimes goes in twice.
solution: Receipts dropped into a Drive folder are read by Claude, which returns supplier, date, total, tax, line items, payment method, category and a confidence level, with null for anything it cannot read. Make checks the sums with formulas and writes a row to the bookkeeping sheet, where a formula also spots possible duplicates. Anything flagged is held back and the bookkeeper is emailed a link to the receipt.
human_check: A person opens every flagged receipt, corrects the row and adds their initials before it counts in the totals.
linkedin_post:
The receipt with the faded total is the one that costs you.

I built a demo for a fictional catering business that photographs supplier receipts and types them into a spreadsheet by hand, usually late at night. Thermal paper fades, totals get misread, and the same slip gets photographed twice.

In the build, a photo or PDF goes into a Drive folder. Claude reads it and returns the supplier, date, total, tax, line items and payment method, with a confidence level for the key values. If something is unreadable it returns null. It is told not to guess and not to work out a missing total.

The checks are not AI. Make compares the total with the line items, and a sheet formula spots possible duplicates. Any row with a low confidence value, a missing total, a mismatch or a duplicate is held back until a person checks the receipt and adds their initials. Only then does it count.

This is a demo build on six sample receipts I generated, not a client project. Link in comments.
